description:
Give the two storage backends one gate-run record reader, with one set of no-follow and clutter rules owned by one conformance test, so the per-issue layout later changes one reader.

## Background

The JSON and memory backends each enumerate the `gate-runs/` root and parse run records with their own no-follow and clutter logic: `crates/jit/src/storage/json.rs:38,959-1043` (`read_gate_runs`) and `:1395-1490`, against `storage/memory.rs:343-380,766-800,909-946`. A repository-file no-follow read already exists (`read_repository_file_nofollow`, `storage/repository_state_store.rs:1810`). The cross-backend conformance suite is `storage/repository_state_store_tests.rs`. Paired backend tests assert the same clutter, symlink and corruption rules per backend, including that a corrupt run of an unrelated issue fails every lookup (`storage/json.rs:1871-2030`; `storage/memory.rs:1032,1061-1160`, through the memory-private helpers `gate_run_vpath`, `gate_run_directory_vpath` and `gate_run_parent_entry` at `:343-380`).

Kept as one change for a build reason: the backend-private enumeration helpers lose their last production caller in this change, and unused crate-private code fails the zero-warning build, so they and the paired tests that call them go here; the paired tests would otherwise re-prove a property the conformance case owns.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Both backends list and load gate-run records through one shared reader built on `read_repository_file_nofollow`; neither backend keeps its own enumeration or no-follow code.
- [hard] REQ-02: One conformance case, run against both backends, owns the clutter and symlink rules for run records and plants records through `VirtualPath::gate_run_record`.
- [hard] REQ-03: The paired per-backend gate-run clutter tests in `json.rs` and `memory.rs` and the memory-private helpers they use no longer exist.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Both storage backends read gate-run records through one reader
